issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s bona fide requirement to use a property to commence a business may sustain an eviction order when the concurrent courts have accepted that requirement and the challenge to it has no substance.
material_facts: The landlord purchased the property apparently so his sons could start a hardware business there.
The landlord sought eviction on the ground of bona fide requirement to commence a business.
The trial court dismissed the eviction petition, but the appellate court accepted the bona fide requirement and the High Court affirmed that decision.
The landlord and tenant were both hardware merchants in the same area.
issues.conclusion: The Court found hardly any substance in the tenant’s challenge and left the eviction order undisturbed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court accepted the concurrent finding that the landlord’s requirement to commence a business was bona fide and rejected the challenge to that finding. It cited no statutory provision or earlier case in deciding this issue.

rule.if: eviction_appeal and landlord_intends_property_for_business and concurrent_courts_accepted_bona_fide_need and challenge_lacks_substance

predicates.eviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an order for eviction.
predicates.landlord_intends_property_for_business: The landlord intends to use the property to commence a business.
predicates.concurrent_courts_accepted_bona_fide_nee: The appellate court and the court reviewing its decision accepted that the landlord had a bona fide need for the property.
predicates.challenge_lacks_substance: The court hearing the appeal found no substantial basis in the challenge to the accepted need.
predicates.eviction_order_upheld: The eviction order remains in force.

issues.definition: When an appeal against eviction challenges a business need accepted by the courts below but the challenge has no substance, the eviction order remains in force.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s long-standing occupation and the hardship of immediate eviction may justify allowing time to surrender possession when the tenant undertakes to vacate by a later date.
material_facts: The tenant had carried on a hardware trade in the premises for 27 years.
The Court considered that outright eviction would cause hardship.
The tenant, through counsel, undertook to give vacant possession by a specified later date.
issues.conclusion: The Court allowed the tenant time to surrender vacant possession and directed that the landlord take no eviction proceedings until that time, relying on the tenant’s undertaking.
issues.legal_principle: The Court granted time in light of the hardship of immediate eviction after long occupation and the tenant’s undertaking to surrender possession. It cited no statutory provision or earlier case in making this order.

rule.if: eviction_appeal and tenant_occupied_for_long_time and immediate_eviction_would_cause_hardship and tenant_undertakes_to_surrender_possession

predicates.eviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an order for eviction.
predicates.tenant_occupied_for_long_time: The tenant has occupied the premises and carried on a business there for a long period.
predicates.immediate_eviction_would_cause_hardship: The court considers that requiring the tenant to leave immediately would cause hardship.
predicates.tenant_undertakes_to_surrender_possessio: The tenant undertakes to give vacant possession by a later date.
predicates.eviction_proceedings_deferred_until_prom: The landlord is directed not to take eviction proceedings until the tenant’s promised surrender of possession.

issues.definition: When a tenant in an eviction appeal has occupied the premises for a long time, immediate eviction would cause hardship, and the tenant undertakes to surrender possession later, eviction proceedings are deferred until the promised surrender.
